title: Finishing the work and letting go

captions.physics: Bringing parts to a shared conclusion
captions.emotions: Becoming bound to a perfect result

meaning: Your ability to complete shared work needs freedom to recognise sufficiency when attachment to perfection keeps you revising.
text: You want a shared result to feel assembled and complete. The World in the physical position of Manipura describes bringing parts together: finishing a sequence, coordinating details and putting an end to the work. The World in energy identifies the motive, reaching the fullness of the idea without leaving anything essential outside. The Devil in emotions shows a possible loss of freedom: attachment to a perfect outcome makes releasing the work difficult. One World concerns completing actions, the other the wish for wholeness, while emotional attachment can keep you beside a result beyond your actual interest.

Imagine finishing the arrangement of a shared board game collection. Everything fits and is easy to find, yet another revision promises more beautiful symmetry. **A finished result leaves you free to stop improving it.** The shelf already fulfils the task you discussed together. You can begin a game instead of giving another evening to an arrangement intended to free time for shared activity.

The difficulty starts if accepting sufficiency feels like abandoning quality. You notice only remaining inconsistencies and postpone using what is ready. Disagreement with another revision sounds like insufficient participation. The whole then binds you to an impossible final perfection. Completion helps when it restores freedom to choose what to do with the result and how to spend time together next.
